title: RHC Canon Intake Promotion Receipt
description: Minimal repository-side promotion receipt for Canon Intake (CI-04): the record of what authoritative route a promotion instruction invoked and the authoritative read-back evidence that route returned. A receipt is evidence, not authority: it never itself performs or authorizes a write, and it exists only to bind a promotion_id to the route actually used, the outcome, and (for success) the exact durable identity read back from the authoritative owner. The schema enforces the closed shape and vocabulary; scripts/validate_intake_promotions.py enforces the route-conditional sufficiency of the evidence. A success receipt for runtime_save must carry runtime_publication evidence identifying a positive published generation and an exact confirmed 40-hex git_ref; a success receipt for repository_canon must carry repository_commit evidence identifying an exact 40-hex repository commit. In both cases the evidence must be verifier-confirmed. A failure receipt carries no success evidence at all, so a failure can never masquerade as success, and a success receipt can never validate without authoritative read-back evidence. There is no generic direct SQL/Git/runtime-published write mechanism here.

receipt_id.description: Stable, typed, set-unique receipt identity: the prefix is always receipt: followed by a lowercase slug. A duplicate receipt_id within one validated promotion set fails closed.

promotion_id.description: Referenced promotion instruction identity, using the exact intake_promotion.schema.json grammar. It must resolve to a valid instruction in the same validated set; an unknown promotion_id fails closed.

candidate_id.description: Referenced CI-01 candidate identity, using the exact intake_candidate.schema.json grammar. It must equal the resolved promotion instruction's candidate_id; a receipt cannot silently re-point the promotion at another candidate.

route.description: The route actually used by the authoritative owner. It must equal the resolved promotion instruction's route; a receipt that reports a different route than the instruction declared fails closed. Closed vocabulary: runtime_save | repository_canon.

outcome.description: The authoritative routed outcome: exactly success or failure. A success receipt requires authoritative read-back evidence for its route; a failure receipt must not carry success evidence. There is no third outcome, no pending, and no optimistic success.

evidence.description: Authoritative verification/read-back evidence. It is a closed object whose fields are route-specific: runtime_publication carries a positive integer generation and the exact confirmed 40-hex runtime-published git_ref; repository_commit carries the exact 40-hex durable repository commit. confirmed must be true: an unconfirmed or unread-back result is never success. Required for a success receipt and forbidden for a failure receipt (enforced by scripts/validate_intake_promotions.py).

kind.description: The authoritative evidence kind: runtime_publication for the RT01 published runtime surface, repository_commit for the repository-authorized canon/static surface.

generation.description: RT01 published generation read back from the runtime surface (positive integer; generation 0 is the empty pre-activation world and is not a publication).

git_ref.description: Exact confirmed 40-hex lowercase runtime-published checkpoint commit SHA read back for the same database-owned generation.

commit.description: Exact 40-hex lowercase durable repository commit SHA read back from the repository-authorized canon/static surface.

confirmed.description: Verifier confirmation marker. It is exactly true: a publication or repository change that was not read back and confirmed for the same identity is not success.

failure_reason.description: Optional non-blank human-readable reason for a failed or incomplete route execution; logistics metadata only and never success evidence.

note.description: Optional non-blank human note about the receipt; logistics metadata only.
